newsitem.title: JORDAN: U.S, Britain pledge money for Palestinian refugees.
newsitem.headline: U.S, Britain pledge money for Palestinian refugees.

text.p: Donor countries pledged on Monday to increase aid to the U.N. Relief Works Agency (UNRWA) to help it tackle a cash shortage threatening services to millions of Palestinian refugees, a U.N. official said.
UNRWA spokesman Sandro Tucci said the United States and Britain announced extra donations to the agency totalling $6.6 million during a one-day meeting in Amman.
Other countries also offered fresh grants, he added.

"The meeting ended successfully," Tucci said. "Host governments and donors reaffirmed their commitment to assisting UNRWA in coping with its structural deficit and trying to meet its immediate financial crisis, to enable the agency to continue its services to the Palestinian refugees."
Final results of Monday's conference would be announced by UNRWA Commissioner General Peter Hansen on Tuesday, he said.
An UNRWA official said on Sunday the organisation was facing a $45 million deficit in its 1996 budget.
But Tucci said UNRWA's 1996 "immediate core deficit", before the new pledges, amounted to $9 million and Monday's assistance should help it meet the current financial crisis.
UNRWA says its financial woes stem from spiralling population growth among 3.3 million registered refugees, scattered around Jordan, the West Bank, Gaza, Lebanon and Syria.
The bulk of UNRWA's $340 million 1996 expenditure goes towards essential education, health, relief and social services to refugees of the 1948 and 1967 Arab-Israeli wars and their children.
